summary.intent: Execute Phase 19.1 (Extract Core Crypto SDK as Shared Package) and verify the SDK integration at the Plan 19.1-05 checkpoint, where web app hooks were rewired to use the new SDK packages.
summary.outcome: Plans 19.1-01 through 19.1-05 were completed with 8 atomic fix commits resolving critical SDK integration bugs discovered via Playwright-driven verification. 9/10 core file system operations work; delete-to-bin falls back to hard delete (known gap).

repo: The project uses a monorepo with pnpm workspaces: @cipherbox/crypto, @cipherbox/core, @cipherbox/api-client, @cipherbox/sdk-core, @cipherbox/sdk, and the web app.
@cipherbox/api-client generated functions require setApiClientConfig() to be called before use — this was never wired into the SDK initialization path, silently breaking all IPNS operations.
The old service layer and new SDK both wrote to the same IPNS records, causing irreconcilable 409 conflicts. The fix was to route all mutations through the SDK exclusively.
Folder entries use a UUID (crypto.randomUUID()) as their id — returning ipnsName as id from createFolder broke store lookups and folder navigation.
The SDK's deleteToBin requires client.loadBin() to be called first; without it, deletes fall back to hard deleteItem silently.
The bin IPNS record created by the old initializeBin service cannot be loaded by the SDK's loadBin due to timing: SDK loadBin fires before the old service creates the bin record.
updateFolderMetadataAndPublish needs a retry on 409 — the old service had withConflictRetry + resyncFolder; the SDK did not.
The web app uses a split-step upload flow (encrypt → upload → create IPNS → register FilePointer) while the SDK handles this atomically; useFileDelete was also not rewired to SDK.
TextEditorDialog imported from the old file-metadata.service path directly rather than going through the download hook, causing decryption failures after SDK migration.
E2E tests can use TEST_LOGIN_SECRET env var to bypass OTP flow for integration testing.

code.finding: setApiClientConfig() must be called here during SDK init, and client.loadBin() must be called after the old initializeBin() service completes — not before.
ensureFolderRegistered should skip sync if SDK already has the folder (has() check), to prevent stale store data from overwriting SDK's up-to-date sequence number and IPNS private key.
createFolder must return the FolderEntry id (UUID) not ipnsName; downstream store uses id for lookups. Also needed downloadFromIpns and getFolderState methods added as public API.
updateFolderMetadataAndPublish needs a 409 retry: re-resolve current IPNS sequence number from API on conflict before retrying publish.
Rewired from two-step old service (encrypt+upload then addFile) to client.uploadFile() — the SDK handles the full atomic operation including IPNS publish.
Rewired from old downloadFromIpns service chain to client.downloadFromIpns() to use the same IPNS resolution path as uploads.
Was importing from old file-metadata.service directly instead of going through the download hook — caused decryption failures. Fixed to use SDK client.
Full SDK lifecycle integration test created: login via TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, create folder, upload, download+verify content, rename file/folder, delete. All 8 operations pass at SDK level.

workflow: The assistant was directed to drive verification via Playwright MCP (headed browser) rather than asking the user to manually test — the user explicitly prefers observing, not driving.
Atomic commits per logical fix (not per file or per wave) are the preferred commit style for this project.
When a GSD checkpoint plan has autonomous: false, the user expects to verify via a Playwright session, not manual browser interaction.
Using random emails per E2E test run prevents state pollution from prior runs — important for IPNS-based storage where sequence numbers must be fresh.
The OTP for dev login is available in API stdout logs and can be extracted with grep on the background task output.
Background Playwright task outputs should be consumed via TaskOutput rather than letting them accumulate.
Playwright MCP (browser_* tools) is preferred over writing playwright spec files for interactive debugging sessions.

friction: The dual-path IPNS write architecture (old service + new SDK both publishing) caused cascading state conflicts that required multiple rounds of debugging — ensureFolderRegistered went through ~5 iterations before being simplified away.
The GSD workflow was interrupted mid-Wave 1 because the user was unhappy with Plan 2 implementation decisions — required full branch reset and re-execution.
E2E test 409 conflicts were hard to distinguish from real SDK bugs vs test environment IPNS cache lag.
The Playwright MCP file upload required writing files to a specific path accessible from the browser context rather than using standard file input selectors.
The assistant kept asking the user to manually verify things — the user had to explicitly redirect to Playwright-driven verification.
classifyHandoffIfNeeded is a known Claude Code runtime bug that can cause false failure reports from subagents after their tool calls complete.
loadBin ordering issue: SDK bin load must happen after old initializeBin completes, but there is no event/hook to signal when the old service is done.
open_items: Delete-to-bin falls back to hard delete — SDK's loadBin cannot resolve the bin IPNS record created by the old service due to initialization ordering. Needs a proper fix.
useFileDelete not rewired to SDK — noted in Plan 19.1-05 checkpoint as architecturally different from folder CRUD, deferred.
Plan 19.1-06 (final cleanup, imports, release config) not executed — the session ended at the 19.1-05 checkpoint.
Pre-existing DTS circular dependency between @cipherbox/core and @cipherbox/crypto causes pnpm -r run build to fail (though per-package builds work).

The debug E2E test file (tests/e2e/tests/sdk-debug.spec.ts) and SDK integration test (packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts) were created as debugging artifacts — decision needed on whether to keep, clean up, or promote to permanent test suite.
useFileUpload still not fully rewired — share re-wrapping logic for uploaded files may differ between old service and SDK paths.
